claim: End-to-end MFU for 7B-MHA and 7B-GQA on 64 A100 GPUs at 128K-1M sequence lengths ranges 0.360-0.518 for the best system, i.e. long-context MFU is comparable to short-context MFU rather than collapsing.
stance_target: the claim that the quadratic FLOPs penalty is paid in wall-clock, not amortized away, for 7B models
scope_conditions: 7B-MHA and 7B-GQA, 64 A100 GPUs, d_sp=64, Selective Checkpoint++, sequence lengths 128K-1M
quoted_support: Table 3. End-to-end training performance (MFU) of 7B-MHA and 7B-GQA on 64 GPUs with d_sp=64 ... 0.360 0.476 0.481 0.389 0.394 0.518 0.518 0.415 0.406

claim: Naive Ring Attention's MFU is under 10% at 128K for 7B-MHA and reaches only 19.6% (GQA) / 40.6% at 1M, so the long-context penalty is dominated by implementation quality rather than by the FLOPs ratio alone.
stance_target: how much of the long-context cost is algorithmic versus implementation
quoted_support: the MFU is less than 10% with the sequence length of 128K ... Specifically in Ring-Attention, the MFU reaches 19.6% with the sequence length of 128K, and increases to 40.6% when the sequence length is 1M.

claim: LoongTrain improves MFU by up to 2.88x versus Megatron-CP and 1.49-1.53x versus DeepSpeed Ulysses, which shows that measured long-context throughput varies by ~3x across implementations at the same FLOPs.
stance_target: the spread of measured long-context throughput across systems
quoted_support: Compared to DS-Ulysses, LoongTrain improves the training performance of MHA and GQA by up to 1.49x and 1.53x, respectively. Compared to Megatron-CP, LoongTrain enhances the performance of MHA and GQA by up to 2.88x and 1.33x, respectively.
